newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-KANU FAVOURITE TO TAKE AFRICAN AWARD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KANU FAVOURITE TO TAKE AFRICAN AWARD.

text.p: Nigeria striker Nwankwo Kanu is sentimental favourite to be named as African Footballer of the Year this weekend despite his playing career coming to an abrupt end.

The 20-year-old Kanu captained Nigeria's under-23 team to the gold medal at the Atlanta Olympics earlier this year but was sidelined soon after when doctors dicovered a heart defect that threatened to kill him if he continued playing.

His crucial goals for Nigeria at the Olympics, combined with a sympathy vote from the Confederation of African Football's panel, is expected to see him become the third Nigerian in four years to win the award.
The award is being made by CAF's technical and press committees and will be announced in Cairo on either Saturday or Sunday, officials have confirmed.
Kanu was due to have an operation in Cleveland, Ohio, last weekend for a heart valve replacement but has had the surgery postponed.

His heart condition was discovered during a routine medical examination at the Italian Institute of Sports Medicine after his transfer from Dutch club Ajax Amsterdam, where he won a European Cup winners' medal, to Internazionale of Italy.
Kanu has also been named among the candidates for the European Footballer of the Year award next month.

Several other Nigerian gold medallists are also in contention for the African award, including 1994 winner Emmanuel Amunike, who scored the winning goal in the Olympic final against Argentina, and midfielder Austin Okocha.
South Africa's African Nations Cup winning team also provides some options with midfielders John Moshoeu and Eric Tinkler and defender Mark Fsh among the outsiders.

Another possible candidate is Tunisian Zoubier Beya, whose classy midfield play helped his country to a surprise place in the Nations Cup final in South Africa in February and is likely to win a CAF Cup medal with his club Etoile du Sahel thi weekend.
